title: Describing people: appearance and mannerisms
subtitle: slender, stocky, unkempt, shrug, scowl
summary: Describe how people look and what their faces and hands are doing, from slender and stocky to grinning, scowling and drumming your fingers.

lesson.heading: Size, weight and build
rows: very tall and thin, usually moving awkwardly
tall with long thin arms and legs and awkward movements; often of boys and men
very fat, in an unhealthy way
with a quite large, solid body; used of men and women
short, and wide across the shoulders and chest

lesson.heading: Using the build adjectives
lesson.text: These words carry strong attitudes. **Slender** is a compliment; **scrawny** is not. **Obese** is a medical word for dangerously fat, while **stout** is much gentler. **Stocky** describes a short, solid, strong body, not a fat one.

examples.text: She introduced me to a tall, **slender** woman who looked very serious.
He was too **scrawny** to be a football player.
My grandfather was a **stocky** man with big hands and broad shoulders.
She's the rather **stout** woman wearing glasses over there.

lesson.heading: Fitness and tidiness
lesson.text: To **bulk up** is to increase in body size, especially by gaining muscle. Someone **lean** is thin and healthy, and someone **wiry** is thin but strong. An **unkempt** person is untidy and scruffy, while someone who never has **a hair out of place** is always neat and smart, with **immaculate** clothes - clothes in perfect condition.

examples.text: Rob has really **bulked up** - he used to be so **lean** and **wiry**, didn't he?

examples.note: kempt does not exist; the opposite is smart or neat

examples.text: His sister was always the opposite - never **a hair out of place** and **immaculate** clothes.

lesson.heading: Complexion
lesson.text: Your **complexion** is the natural colour and condition of the skin on your face. A **swarthy** complexion is dark-coloured; a **sallow** one is rather yellowish and unhealthy-looking. Someone who looks **haggard** has a face that looks ill and tired.

examples.text: He has a rather **swarthy** complexion: his sister's was more **sallow**.
I must say he looked a bit **haggard** and exhausted too.
Dan hasn't slept for three days - he looks really tired and **haggard**!

lesson.heading: Facial expressions
rows: position your lips in an attractive way, or in a look of annoyance
make an expression of pain or strong dislike
look at someone in an unpleasant, sexually interested way

lesson.heading: Expressions in use
lesson.text: Notice that **pout** has two quite different senses: models **pout** for the camera to look attractive, but a child **pouts** to show annoyance. A **scowl** shows anger or irritation, and to **leer** at someone is always unpleasant.

examples.text: *A:* What are you **grinning** at? *B:* You've got ice cream on your nose!
If her daughter doesn't get what she wants, she **pouts** for the rest of the day.
You don't have to **grimace** every time I eat raw garlic. I happen to think it's delicious.
I arrived late and she just **scowled** at me.

lesson.heading: Mannerisms and actions
lesson.text: You **shrug your shoulders** to show you do not know or do not care. You **fold your arms** (one arm over the other close to the body) and **cross your legs** while sitting. Nervous people **twitch**, **bite their nails**, or **tap** or **drum** their fingers on the table. An angry person **clenches a fist** - closes the hand tightly.

examples.text: I asked him for advice but he just **shrugged his shoulders**.
He **folded his arms** and **crossed his legs** and waited for me to speak.
He sat there **twitching** nervously as he waited for his interview.
She **clenched her fist** and told him to get out of the room at once.
He just kept **tapping** his fingers on the table, looking impatient.
examples.note: drumming your fingers means the same

lesson.text: Lean and wiry is a compliment - thin, healthy and strong. Scrawny for the same body shape is an insult.

exercises.prompt: She looks as if she needs a good meal; her body is so ___.
exercises.explanation: Scrawny means unattractively thin and bony-looking.

exercises.prompt: Martha and David are both rather ___ individuals - very tall and thin.
exercises.explanation: Lanky means very tall and thin, and usually moving awkwardly.
Obese is the medical word for dangerously overweight.

exercises.prompt: A ___ boy with long, thin arms and legs carried our bags for us.
exercises.explanation: Gangling or gangly describes a tall boy or man with long thin limbs and awkward movements.

exercises.prompt: Her new silk dress suited her ___ frame.
exercises.explanation: Slender means thin in an attractive way.

exercises.prompt: A ___ man with broad shoulders offered to lift the stone so we could look underneath.
exercises.explanation: Stocky means short and wide across the shoulders and chest.

exercises.prompt: That solid-looking woman on the left is Charlie's wife - the rather ___ one.
exercises.hint: (begins with st, used of men and women)
exercises.explanation: Stout describes a quite large, solid body and is gentler than fat.

exercises.prompt: Finn looked really ___ after two weeks of camping - his clothes were dirty and his hair was a mess!
exercises.explanation: Unkempt means untidy and scruffy. There is no word kempt.

exercises.prompt: Leah always looks amazing - she never has a ___ out of place!
exercises.explanation: Never a hair out of place means always well-dressed, neat and smart-looking.

exercises.prompt: Alex has ___ a lot - it must be all that time he spends at the gym lifting weights!
exercises.explanation: To bulk up is to increase in body size, especially by gaining muscle.

exercises.prompt: Sam holds his hand closed very tightly because he is furious. What is he doing?
exercises.explanation: You clench your fist when you feel really angry or frustrated.

exercises.prompt: Mia lifts her shoulders up and down to show she has no idea. What is she doing?
exercises.explanation: People shrug their shoulders to show they don't know, or don't care.

exercises.prompt: Leo makes quick, light hitting movements on the table because he is impatient. What is he doing?
exercises.explanation: You tap or drum your fingers on a table when you are nervous or impatient.

exercises.prompt: If someone scowls at you, how are they probably feeling?
exercises.explanation: A scowl is a bad-tempered, angry look.

exercises.prompt: If someone is described as lean and wiry, they are ___.
exercises.explanation: Lean means thin and healthy; wiry means thin but strong.

exercises.statement: A sallow complexion is dark-coloured and a swarthy one is yellowish.
exercises.explanation: It is the other way round: a swarthy complexion is dark, a sallow one is rather yellowish and unhealthy-looking.

exercises.statement: The verb pout can describe both an attractive look for a photographer and a look of annoyance.
exercises.explanation: Correct - models pout for the camera, and a child pouts when it does not get what it wants.

exercises.prompt: Match each verb with what the person is doing.

pairs.right: show pain or strong dislike on your face
look at someone in an unpleasant, sexually interested way
cross one arm over the other close to your body

exercises.prompt: Does each word describe how someone looks, or something they do with their face or hands?

exercises.answer: He used to be so lean and wiry, didn't he?
exercises.explanation: Lean and wiry is a fixed pair meaning thin, healthy and strong.
